name: sites
description:
In sorted order, show the registry’s site identifiers.

Returns:
    SitesResult: Unique site identifiers, with `["MAIN"]` substituted if the registry
    contains no entries.

name: asset_ids
description:
For a site, show its registered asset identifiers.

For registry metadata as well, choose `assets()`.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.

Returns:
    AssetsResult: Asset identifiers in sorted order, together with their count.

name: asset_detail
description:
For an individual asset, retrieve its registry details.

Identity, type, description, location, status, installation date,
vintage plus the installed-sensor total are included. For names, use `installed_sensors()`.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.
    asset_id: From `asset_ids()`, take an exact identifier, e.g. `Chiller 6`.

Returns:
    AssetDetail: Registry fields available, with optional values set to null
    if missing.

name: measured_sensors
description:
For asset telemetry, show the observed measurement fields.

The full stream yields a sorted union; record metadata is omitted.
Assigned sensor names, potentially different, come from `installed_sensors()`.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.
    asset_id: From `asset_ids()`, take an exact identifier, e.g. `Chiller 6`.

Returns:
    SensorsResult: Names of observed measurement names, together with their count.

name: installed_sensors
description:
For an asset, show the sensor names assigned in its registry.

For observed telemetry fields, choose `measured_sensors()`; the lists can
be different.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.
    asset_id: From `asset_ids()`, take an exact identifier, e.g. `Chiller 6`.

Returns:
    SensorsResult: Names and their count, following the registry’s order.

name: assets
description:
With brief registry metadata, show assets registered at a site.

For identifiers alone, choose `asset_ids()`; additional fields come from `asset_detail()`
for an individual asset.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.
    assettype: For exact matching with case preserved, optionally filter by type, e.g.
        `PUMP`, alternatively `COMPRESSOR`.

Returns:
    AssetsWithMetadataResult: In identifier order, assets include description,
    type, vintage plus the total of installed sensors.

name: find_assets_by_sensors
description:
Using observed or assigned sensor names, locate site assets.

Search is confined to registered assets under `site_name`. Repeated queries are
removed in order of their initial occurrence.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.
    sensors: With `substring` enabled, fragments; otherwise sensor names.
    match: Each query must match for `all`; one or more suffice for `any`.
    substring: Replace exact comparison with case-insensitive fragments, instead of
        case-sensitive whole-name matching.
    source: Observed fields use `measured`; `installed` checks
        registry sensor assignments. The default remains `measured`.

Returns:
    FindAssetsResult: Matched assets and query settings, accompanied by the actual
    names of matching sensors.

name: stream_extent
description:
For asset telemetry, inspect the record count and timestamp extent.

A measured sensor and ISO 8601 half-open interval can optionally filter results:
Include `start`, exclude `end`. Records filtered by sensor qualify
only with a present, non-null field. Observation timestamps and bounds
must uniformly omit or include timezone offsets; offset-aware timestamps undergo
instant-based comparison even with differing offsets.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.
    asset_id: From `asset_ids()`, take an exact identifier, e.g. `Chiller 6`.
    sensor: From `measured_sensors()`, an optional exact field identifier.
        Reserved metadata identifiers, including `asset_id` and `timestamp`, cannot be
        used as sensor identifiers.
    start: As an date or datetime formatted using ISO 8601, an optional included lower boundary.
    end: As an date or datetime formatted using ISO 8601, an optional excluded upper boundary.

Returns:
    StreamExtentResult: Qualifying first/last timestamps, plus record
    count, an indication of exceeding a page of 1000 records, and average
    spacing derived from the temporal extent and count.

name: history
description:
For an asset, fetch a chronologically ordered page of telemetry.

A ISO 8601 half-open interval optionally bounds results. Through `sensors`, select
precise measured fields; omission includes every measured field present per
row. Rows retain `asset_id` and `timestamp`, excluding all other record
metadata.

On the initial page, omit `cursor`; a true `has_more` requires resubmitting the
identical query using `next_cursor`; each cursor is opaque, query-specific. Timestamp
offsets follow the rules of `stream_extent()`.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.
    asset_id: From `asset_ids()`, take an exact identifier, e.g. `Chiller 6`.
    start: An included lower boundary in ISO 8601, optionally supplied.
    end: An excluded upper boundary in ISO 8601, optionally supplied.
    sensors: Exact measured names in an optional nonempty list. Repeated
        names are deduplicated, with their original order preserved.
    limit: Between 1 and 1000 observations at most per page.
    cursor: From this identical query’s preceding page, its opaque `next_cursor`.

Returns:
    HistoryResult: Observations after projection with their count and echoed boundaries,
    plus cursor fields to access the subsequent page.

name: latest_reading
description:
For an asset, fetch its most recent telemetry observation.

Without `sensor`, include every measured field of the latest record. If a sensor is
specified, its field must be non-null and present in the most recent qualifying record.
The tool orders records by parsed timestamps, following `stream_extent()`.

`age_seconds` expresses current UTC time minus the observation
timestamp. Timestamps lacking offsets are treated as UTC; negative age
signifies that the timestamp lies ahead of now.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.
    asset_id: From `asset_ids()`, take an exact identifier, e.g. `Chiller 6`.
    sensor: From `measured_sensors()`, an optional exact field identifier. Reserved
        metadata identifiers cannot serve as sensors.

Returns:
    LatestReadingResult: Chosen values and timestamp, with age measured in seconds.

name: sensor_coverage
description:
For each measured sensor, summarize coverage excluding null observations.

The entire timestamped stream is scanned. `non_null_count` counts any present,
values that are non-null, irrespective of type. Fields seen exclusively as null receive zero
count with null boundaries; offset treatment follows `stream_extent()`.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.
    asset_id: From `asset_ids()`, take an exact identifier, e.g. `Chiller 6`.

Returns:
    SensorCoverageResult: Counts per sensor and scanned timestamped-record total
    with chronological boundaries, ordered by field name.

name: sensor_stats
description:
For all measured sensors or one, calculate numerical summaries.

Without `sensor`, each measured field is summarized. Optional bounds define a
ISO 8601 half-open interval; offset treatment follows `stream_extent()`.

The numerical summaries include finite numbers and strings representing numbers.
Present non-finite, non-numeric, boolean and null values enter
`null_count`; neither count includes absent fields. Here, `stddev` denotes
population standard deviation, yielding `0.0` with a single numeric observation, null with none.

Args:
    site_name: For an exact identifier such as `MAIN`, `sites()` can
        show the valid site identifiers.
    asset_id: From `asset_ids()`, take an exact identifier, e.g. `Chiller 6`.
    sensor: From `measured_sensors()`, an optional exact field identifier; omission will
        summarize each measured field.
    start: An included lower boundary in ISO 8601, optionally supplied.
    end: An excluded upper boundary in ISO 8601, optionally supplied.

Returns:
    SensorStatsResult: Field-specific range and mean, counts of numeric/null values,
    population standard deviation, plus first/last timestamps of numeric observations.

name: json_reader
description: After opening and parsing a JSON file, provides the resulting data.

name: get_sensor_catalog
description:
From the catalog, retrieve sensor types.

With `sensor` plus `description`, entries cover every cataloged
sensor type when sensor is omitted; supply sensor for exact name matching.

name: get_asset_catalog
description:
From the catalog, retrieve asset classes with their categories.

Each entry includes `category`, `category_description`, `asset`, plus
`description`; retrieve the full class catalog without filters, or supply
asset, category, or both to request exact matching.

name: get_failure_mode_catalog
description:
By asset category, retrieve cataloged failure modes.

With `category`, `failure_mode`, plus `description`, entries are unfiltered
to enumerate every cataloged mode; alternatively supply failure_mode, category, or both
to request exact matching.

name: current_date_time
description: In JSON, provides the present date together with time.

name: current_time_english
description: Using English wording, gives the present time.

name: get_failure_modes
description:
For a specified asset class, READ its known failure modes.

Args:
    asset_class: Requested class, e.g. "pump". Case and whitespace, together with
        digits, hyphens and underscores, are normalized before lookup.

name: generate_failure_modes
description:
For a specified asset class, GENERATE a failure-mode list, fresh or expanded.

No database writes occur. If normalized `asset_class`
is already stored, the saved modes provide context
for additional modes from the LLM. Without stored modes, the LLM
produces a fresh list.

Args:
    asset_class: Requested class for reasoning, e.g. "pump". Letter case,
        whitespace, digits, hyphens and underscores are normalized before
        sending the LLM prompt.
    max_modes: From the LLM, the maximum requested quantity of newly generated failure modes.

name: add_failure_modes
description:
For a specified asset class, WRITE failure modes into the database.

The tool merges incoming modes without case sensitivity, preserving existing modes,
and reports exclusively the additions. Use when generated or curated
modes should be retrievable through later `get_failure_modes` retrieval.

Args:
    asset_class: Requested class for modification, e.g. "pump". Case and whitespace, with
        digits, hyphens and underscores, are normalized before persistence.
    failure_modes: For this asset class, modes to add.
    exhaustive: Only a stored set believed complete warrants true. When
        unspecified, new records default to false while existing records retain their value.
    source: For the stored set, optional provenance.

name: list_workorders
description:
By site, asset, status, priority or dates, optionally filter work orders.
With page_size=0, every match returns together; status allows OPEN / APPROVED_PENDING.

name: get_workorder
description: Using site plus number, fetch one work order.

name: get_workorder_tasks
description: Show a work-order’s subordinate tasks.

name: get_workorder_costs
description: For one work order, show actual spending on labor, material, service and tools.

name: get_workorder_actuals_vs_planned
description: Give work-order variances in hours and costs: actuals versus estimates.

name: get_workorder_kpis
description: Priority/asset distributions, mean completion, totals, backlog and overdue work: site KPIs.

name: get_schedule_calendar
description: Within a time window, group non-terminal scheduled work orders by day.

name: get_my_assigned_workorders
description: Using labor code, show work orders allocated to that technician.

name: get_failure_codes
description:
From CouchDB, read the FCC reference catalog of failure codes.

With ``code`` unspecified, enumerate every available failure code; supply an exact code
like ``FC001`` for matching without case sensitivity; CouchDB metadata is excluded
from results.

name: generate_work_order
description: Attach aob_source agent/trigger/evidence provenance when creating a work order with WAPPR status.

name: update_workorder
description: For a work order, modify editable fields.

name: approve_workorder
description: Set APPR through work-order approval.

name: assign_technician
description: Add a wplabor entry to assign a technician.

name: close_workorder
description: Record actuals plus resolution while closing a work order into COMP.

name: cancel_workorder
description: Into CAN, cancel the work order.
